why: A national car rental firm spending up to €50m upfront and €400k to €650k a month for 700 to 1,600 extra rentals a day at €19 to €26 profit each is believable.
Household incomes of roughly $4,600 to $43,000 at market rates, with PPP rates below the exchange rates, are believable for a spread of launch markets.
A supermarket chain putting $3m to $18m of yearly regional profit at risk, with 10% to 50% odds of a discounter arriving, is believable.
Advertising spending growth between -7.3% and 9.7% across countries, with letter ratings and censorship scores, is believable.
Both pies add to 100% and 2,600 reply cards in a month from a restored steam railway's passengers is believable.
A household energy supplier's call centre taking 2,300 to 5,600 calls a weekday, with none at weekends when it is closed, is believable.
Mobile payments adding 0.2 to 0.7 percentage points of GDP growth per sector over 10 years, with direct and indirect parts summing to the stated tips, is believable.
All four pies add to 100%, and 1,040 respondents being 13% of downtown members implies about 8,000 members, believable for a gym chain.
Offshore fields forgoing $6m to $32m of crude in a storm shutdown, with 10% to 40% odds a season, is believable.
All four score distributions add to 100% and survey samples of 1,420 and 960 helpline callers are believable for an electricity supplier.
